mission.brief: Replace stale content in overwrite.txt with part1.txt. Extend append.txt with part2.txt once. Finish with overwrite.txt containing alpha and append.txt containing alpha then beta. Read both final reports after all writes.
constraints: Only simulated UTF-8 text. No host shell, files, processes or network.
Use Command reference for the exact supported subset; no regex, globbing, variables, escapes or unsupported options. Quotes group literal words.
Locale is C: bytewise sorting and ASCII word separators. wc -c counts UTF-8 bytes; wc -l counts LF characters.
Inspection goals require the named tool and exact displayed result from the relevant source; equivalent supported paths and approaches count.
Only declared report destinations may be written. > truncates before input is read; errors do not undo writes. >> appends.
Any actual write clears earlier verification. Finish changes before inspecting the final outputs. Final report grading does not require one exact transcript.

objectives.label: Final report: overwrite.txt is alpha only
Final report: append.txt is alpha then beta

hints: One destination needs replacement, the other needs one append.
> is destructive to previous output even if the command later fails. >> can accidentally duplicate records.
cat part1.txt > overwrite.txt; cat part2.txt >> append.txt; then read both outputs. Enter each separately; semicolons unsupported.

lesson.goal: Replace stale content in overwrite.txt with part1.txt. Extend append.txt with part2.txt once. Finish with overwrite.txt containing alpha and append.txt containing alpha then beta. Read both final reports after all writes.

steps.explanation: > opens and truncates the output before reading input. A bad source still erases old content; verify paths first.
>> retains existing text and adds stdout. Repeating it would add a second beta and fail the exact final-state goal.
Inspect after all writes: writes clear previous stream verification.
Verify contents rather than assuming an earlier redirect succeeded.
